Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries is expected to be selected as House speaker in the 120th Congress [J Scott Applewhite/AP Photo]By Tamara KhandakerPublished On 5 Nov 20265 Nov 2026
Democrats rode a blue wave to victory in the United States midterm elections, winning control of both chambers of Congress. Now comes the question of whether they can deliver on their promises.
The party campaigned on bringing down the cost of living, ending the war on Iran and holding President Donald Trump accountable, as well as pushing back against his immigration crackdown.
Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Hakeem Jeffries promises ‘affordability’ focus after Democratic midterm winlist 2 of 4Democratic progressive wing notches win in California Central Valleylist 3 of 4Iranians celebrate Democrat victory in US midtermslist 4 of 4Democrat leaders hail midterm election successend of list
But Democrats won’t take control of Congress until January. Even then, there’s only so much they’ll be able to do without Republican cooperation.
Most bills need 60 votes to get past a filibuster in the Senate, and even if Democrats manage that, Trump can still veto their legislation. He has already threatened to do just that, telling a podcast on Monday, “I’ll veto everything.”
But the Democrats now also have other tools at their disposal, including power over Senate confirmations and control over committees that can launch investigations.
So what can Democrats realistically accomplish over the next two years, and where might they struggle to make good on their promises?
Can Democrats bring down the cost of living?

Workers assess damage at the Al-Markhiyat power station north of Omdurman, Sudan, following a reported drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) [File: AFP]By AP and ReutersPublished On 4 Nov 20264 Nov 2026
Ethiopia has ordered six Sudanese diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours and closed Sudan’s consulate in the border town of Asosa, according to media reports.
The reports on Tuesday came as tensions between the countries continue to rise, with Sudan accusing Addis Ababa of ⁠supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which is fighting the Sudanese army, while Ethiopia accuses Khartoum of backing rebels in its northern Tigray region.

The allegations and counter-allegations, which both ⁠sides deny, have raised fears that Ethiopia’s and Sudan’s wars could bleed into each other, spawning a broader conflict in the Horn of Africa.
The Reuters news agency, citing a senior Ethiopian official, reported on Tuesday that Ethiopia ordered six staff members of the Sudanese consulate in the border town ⁠of Asosa to leave within 48 hours. It said the official asked not to be named in order to discuss a sensitive diplomatic matter.
The Associated Press news agency also reported the action, citing an Ethiopian intelligence official. It also said a Sudanese official had corroborated the expulsions, adding that Ethiopian authorities had summoned Sudan’s ambassador on Sunday to announce the consulate’s closure.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, left, laughs with US Senator Bernie Sanders, right, during an address marking Mamdani's first 100 days in office on Sunday, April 12, 2026 [File: Andres Kudacki/AP]By Umar FarooqPublished On 4 Nov 20264 Nov 2026
A record number of candidates for federal offices who were backed by or affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) won in Tuesday’s US midterm elections, marking the most successful night the left-leaning movement has had in national politics so far.
“This is a record for the DSA; these are numbers we have not seen in over a hundred years in socialist electoral activity,” National Electoral Commission member Chanpreet Singh said on a livestream on Tuesday night after the elections. The stream, broadcast on Twitch to more than 200,000 viewers, was hosted by political commentator Hasan Piker.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What does Mamdani’s win mean for the future of the Democratic Party?list 2 of 3Zohran Mamdani wins: Who are the Democratic Socialists of America?list 3 of 3Mamdani’s progressive allies vie for seats in Congressend of list
The political group saw a surge in membership in 2016, when Vermont’s US Senator Bernie Sanders, a prominent DSA member, ran unsuccessfully for president, bringing the movement’s views on issues like universal healthcare and housing to a broader audience. The election of Zohran Mamdani as mayor of New York City in 2025 brought more attention, and more members, to the DSA.

Mansour Gaily walks in his factory in Omdurman, Sudan [N. Mahmoud/Al Jazeera]By N. MahmoudPublished On 4 Nov 20264 Nov 2026
Khartoum, Sudan – Mansour Gaily’s factory in Khartoum produced sweets for local consumers and provided employment for workers.
But when fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, production ground to a halt, like thousands of other businesses across the country.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Darfur survivors vow to tell story of those killed after Sudan camp attackslist 2 of 3Deadly RSF drone attacks reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopialist 3 of 3Sudan’s displaced return to new challenges in war-battered Khartoumend of list
More than three years later, Gaily faces the challenge of bringing his business back to life. Production may have resumed, but the factory is only operating at 40 percent of its previous capacity.
“Our losses are estimated at $1m,” Gaily told Al Jazeera. “We lost some machinery, spare parts, and needed to rebuild large parts of the factory.”
Gaily’s troubles are typical of Sudan’s devastated manufacturing sector. Before the war, Khartoum was one of the country’s main industrial centres, home to factories producing food, textiles and other consumer goods.
However, Khartoum became a major battleground between the SAF and the RSF during the war, and although there have only been sporadic attacks since the army fully recaptured it last year, the industrial sector has not been rebuilt.
According to Sudan’s Ministry of Industry, approximately 1,800 industrial facilities have been damaged during the war, including 650 factories that were completely destroyed.
